pll1d19c5-d1e3477.summary: States that no person is a part of God or of the divine essence, since each is true and full God and the whole essence; so none is a part in the Trinity.
claims: No person is a part of God.
Each person is the whole divine essence.

pll1d19c5-d1e3480.summary: Cites Augustine against Maximinus: Maximinus fears that if the three are one God, the Father would be part of a God composed of three, but there is no division of parts in the unity of deity. The Trinity is one God, and the Father is not part of God.
claims: There is no division of parts in the Godhead.
The Father is not a part of God.

pl-l1d19c5.summary: Holds that no person is a part of God or of the divine essence, since each is true and full God and the whole essence. Augustine against Maximinus: there is no division of parts in the unity of the Godhead; the Trinity is one God, and the Father is not part of God.
claims: No person of the Trinity is a part of God or of the divine essence.
Each person is true and full God and the whole divine essence.
There is no division into parts in the Godhead.
